Security.0103.description: Certificate management packages or configurations detected. This may indicate the application is using local or custom certificate handling, which could require adjustments when migrating to Azure. Consider using Azure Key Vault Certificates for secure storage, lifecycle management, and integration with Azure services.
Security.0103.title: Certificate management dependency detected

Scale.0001.description:
Static content detected.

Your current approach of serving static content directly might lead to increased costs, performance issues, maintenance challenges (requiring application redeployment for content changes), and security risks.

Consider moving static content to Azure Blob Storage and adding Azure CDN.
Scale.0001.title: Static content detected

Database.0002.description:
SQL database connection detected.

Ensure the database is available/reachable on Azure.

If it is not, there are multiple ways you can move your data to Azure:
    1. Migrate to Azure SQL Database.
    2. Consider Azure SQL Managed Instance if you need features that are not available in Azure SQL Database and you don’t want to use a VM.
    3. Migrate your database servers directly to SQL Server on Azure VMs.

To assess database migration effort, you can use Azure Migrate tool, see the link below.
Database.0002.title: SQL database connection detected

links.title: Migrate SQL Server database to Azure

Database.0003.description:
System.Data.SqlClient dependency is detected.

While System.Data.SqlClient will work in Azure, the newer Microsoft.Data.SqlClient package is the primary .NET SQL client moving forward and receiving the latest features. For example, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient easily allows use of Azure Managed Identity from a connection string.
Database.0003.title: System.Data.SqlClient dependency detected

Identity.0002.description:
Your app is using windows authentication which is not supported on Azure App Service, Azure Container Apps and Azure Kubernetes Service.

Azure App Service provides built-in authentication and authorization capabilities, so you can sign in users and access data by writing minimal or no code in your web app.

Follow the link below for more information."
Identity.0002.title: Windows authentication detected

Security.0003.description:
Hardcoded sensitive data detected.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, externalize secrets to Key Vault/App Configuration; use managed identity instead of passwords or embedded connection strings.

While if targeting other Azure compute services:

Avoid placing sensitive data such as passwords, ids, tokens etc., directly in config files and code since it compromises the security of your application.

Use Azure App Configuration or Azure KeyVault to store secrets.
Security.0003.title: Hardcoded sensitive data detected

Local.0006.description:
Your application has hardcoded URLs that might correspond to services that are not accessible on Azure.

Review and ensure that the application is attempting to access URLs that would be available from Azure. You might need to migrate those services to Azure too, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.

If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premises, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local.0006.title: Hardcoded URLs detected

evidence.explanation:
[CVE-2026-40021](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4f7c-pmjv-c25w): Apache Log4net: Silent log event loss in XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J due to unescaped XML 1.0 forbidden characters

Severity: MEDIUM

Apache Log4net's  XmlLayout https://logging.apache.org/log4net/manual/configuration/layouts.html#layout-list  and  XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J https://logging.apache.org/log4net/manual/configuration/layouts.html#layout-list , in versions before 3.3.0, fail to sanitize characters forbidden by the  XML 1.0 specification https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#charsets  in MDC property keys and values, as well as the identity field that may carry attacker-influenced data. This causes an exception during serialization and the silent loss of the affected log event.

An attacker who can influence any of these fields can exploit this to suppress individual log records, impairing audit trails and detection of malicious activity.

Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Log4net 3.3.0, which fixes this issue.

Affected dependencies:
  - log4net:2.0.12 (packages.config:10); range < 3.3.0; patched 

Recommended fix: upgrade log4net to 3.3.0 or later.

evidence.explanation:
[CVE-2024-21319](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-59j7-ghrg-fj52): Microsoft ASP.NET Core project templates vulnerable to denial of service

Severity: MEDIUM

A Denial of Service vulnerability exists in ASP.NET Core project templates which utilize JWT-based authentication tokens. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated client to consume arbitrarily large amounts of server memory, potentially triggering an out-of-memory condition on the server and making the server no longer able to respond to legitimate requests. 

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at  https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/290

### Mitigation factors

This impacts only .NET Core-based projects that were created using any version of project templates listed in affected software. 
Other project templates e.g., console applications, MAUI applications, Windows Forms or WPF applications, are not affected.

## Affected software

This impacts only .NET Core-based projects that were created using any version of the below project templates.

-	ASP.NET Core Web App (Model-View-Controller)
-	ASP.NET Core Web API
-	ASP.NET Core Web App (Razor Pages)
-	Blazor Server App
-	Blazor WebAssembly App

## Advisory FAQ

### How do I know if I am affected?

If you are you using project templates listed in affected software, you may be exposed to the vulnerability.

### How do I fix the issue?

#### For existing projects:
If you ever created any of these projects via the dotnet new command or via Visual Studio's File -> New Project gesture, and if you enabled federated authentication at project creation time, your project may be vulnerable. To remediate the vulnerability, use your package manager to update any references you may have to the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect, and Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens packages to their respective latest versions. 
- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer/) 
- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect/) 

If your project does not reference any of those three packages, you are not exposed to this vulnerability.

#### For new projects:
To remediate this issue please update to the latest SDK listed below. Simply installing the SDK update is not sufficient to remediate projects already-created / already-deployed projects which existed prior to this update being released.

* To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET 6.0 or .NET 7.0. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET  SDKs.
* If you are using one of the affected packages, please update to the patched version listed above.
* If you have .NET 6.0 or greater installed, you can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. You will see output like the following;

```
.NET Core SDK (reflecting any global.json):

 Version:   7.0.200
 Commit:    8473146e7d

Runtime Environment:

 OS Name:     Windows
 OS Version:  10.0.18363
 OS Platform: Windows
 RID:         win10-x64
 Base Path:   C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk\7.0.300\

Host (useful for support):

  Version: 76.0.5
  Commit:  8473146e7d

.NET Core SDKs installed:

  7.0.200 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk]

.NET Core runtimes installed:

  Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 7.0.5 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.AspNetCore.App]
  Microsoft.NETCore.App 7.0.5 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.NETCore.App]
  Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App 7.0.5 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App]

To install additional .NET Core runtimes or SDKs:
  https://aka.ms/dotnet-download
```

* If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.101 SDK (for Visual Studio 2022 v17.8) from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0.
* If you're using .NET 7.0, you should download and install .NET SDK 7.0.115 (for Visual Studio 2022 v17.4) from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/7.0.
* If you're using .NET 6.0, you should download and install .NET SDK 6.0.321 (for Visual Studio 2022 v17.2) from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/6.0.

.NET 6.0, .NET 7.0, .NET 8.0 updates are also available from Microsoft Update. To access this either type "Check for updates" in your Windows search, or open Settings, choose Update & Security and then click Check for Updates.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

## Other Information

### Reporting Security Issues

If you have found a potential security issue in .NET 8.0 or .NET 7.0 or .NET 6.0, please email details to secure@microsoft.com. Reports may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Core & .NET 5 Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at <https://aka.ms/corebounty>.

### Support

You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime and https://github.com/dotnet/aspnet/. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue.

### Disclaimer

In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply.

### Acknowledgement

Affected dependencies:
  - System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt:5.6.0 (packages.config:97); range < 5.7.0; patched 
  - System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt:5.6.0 (packages.config:97); range >= 6.5.0, < 6.34.0; patched 
  - System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt:5.6.0 (packages.config:97); range >= 7.0.0-preview, < 7.1.2; patched 
  - Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens:5.6.0 (packages.config:51); range < 5.7.0; patched 
  - Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens:5.6.0 (packages.config:51); range >= 6.5.0, < 6.34.0; patched 
  - Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens:5.6.0 (packages.config:51); range >= 7.0.0-preview, < 7.1.2; patched 

Recommended fix: upgrade affected Microsoft.IdentityModel.JsonWebTokens and System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt packages from 5.6.0 to 5.7.0 or later, and verify the advisory applicability for this .NET Framework MVC deployment.

evidence.explanation: GetSequenceIdFromSelectedDBSequence casts the SQL sequence result from Int64 to int without a range check at CatalogDBInitializer.cs:327. The sequence is declared AS bigint at dbo.catalog_hilo.Sequence.sql:5, so values above Int32.MaxValue can be truncated when assigned as catalog IDs.

security.title: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
security.description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.

evidence.explanation: The Index action accepts pageSize and pageIndex from query parameters without bounds and passes them through. CatalogService multiplies them for Skip and uses pageSize for Take; the view model divides by pageSize and casts the ceiling to int. Zero, negative, or extreme values can produce a divide-by-zero/overflow or incorrect pagination results.

security.title: Incorrect Calculation
security.description: The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.

evidence.explanation: UpLoadImageFromFile opens a FileStream with File.OpenRead at line 111, uploads it at line 116, and exits without disposing the stream. Repeated catalog initialization can retain file handles and resources.

security.title: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: UpLoadImageFromFile opens a file handle with File.OpenRead at line 111 and never closes or disposes it after UploadFromStream at line 116, so repeated calls can exhaust file handles.

security.title: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: The public Index action accepts an unbounded pageSize query parameter and passes it to CatalogService, which calls Take(pageSize).ToList() without a maximum. A very large pageSize can cause a large database result to be materialized in memory.

security.title: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
security.description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.

evidence.explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a SingleInstance. The singleton owns a mutable List<CatalogItem> shared across concurrent web requests.

security.title: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

evidence.explanation: CatalogServiceMock mutates and reads its shared catalogItems list in create, update, and remove operations without synchronization. Concurrent requests can race while reading or modifying the list.

security.title: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: The singleton mock catalog is shared across request threads, but its list operations are not protected by a lock or concurrent collection, allowing simultaneous access during writes and reads.

security.title: Improper Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

evidence.explanation: The shared mutable catalogItems list is accessed by request methods without synchronization. A lock exists in CatalogItemHiLoGenerator for a different resource, but it does not guard this list.

security.title: Missing Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

evidence.explanation: The checked-in local Docker Compose override sets a literal SQL Server SA password for the database container and repeats it in the health-check command; the application connection string also uses the built-in SA credential. These are development credentials stored in plaintext configuration, not secret references.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Password
security.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: InitializeCatalogImages sets the entire pics blob container to BlobContainerPublicAccessType.Blob (public blob reads). The same container receives temporary user uploads via UploadTempImage, and the PicController upload action has no local authorization attribute, so uploaded temporary blobs are also publicly readable by URL.

security.title: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
security.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

evidence.explanation: The sign-in action logs only a generic entry message before challenging OpenID Connect. It does not record the authentication result or principal, so successful and failed authentication outcomes are not auditable from the application log.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: The checked-in local Docker Compose override sets a literal SQL Server SA password for the database container and repeats it in the health-check command; the application connection string also uses the built-in SA credential. These are development credentials stored in plaintext configuration, not secret references.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
security.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
